absolute-convergence.def: A series $\sum a_n$ converges absolutely when $\sum |a_n|$ converges. Absolute convergence implies convergence, and the sum does not change when the terms are rearranged.

conditional-convergence.def: A series converges conditionally when $\sum a_n$ converges but $\sum |a_n|$ diverges, as $\sum \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$ does.
